questions.stem: A claims process follows six fixed validation steps with one bounded language judgment. Which architecture is proportionate?

options.text: A deterministic workflow that calls Claude only for the language judgment
options.rationale: Stable steps benefit from explicit control while Claude handles the uncertain subtask.

options.text: A fully autonomous agent choosing every step
options.rationale: Autonomy adds cost and variability without open-ended planning needs.

options.text: A five-agent debate for every claim
options.rationale: Consensus is disproportionate to a routine process.

options.text: One prompt with no validation
options.rationale: A monolithic prompt removes required deterministic checks.

questions.stem: A custom agent loop receives stop_reason=tool_use with two tool blocks. What should the implementation do next?

options.text: Treat the response as final text
options.rationale: tool_use signals that execution and a follow-up model turn are required.

options.text: Execute authorized calls, append matching tool_result blocks, then call Claude again
options.rationale: This is the required request-execute-return loop.

options.text: Drop the assistant tool-use message from history
options.rationale: Tool results must correspond to the assistant requests in context.

options.text: Retry the identical request without tools
options.rationale: Retrying does not complete the requested operations.

questions.stem: A long code-review agent fills its context with raw file contents and loses the original criteria. Which pattern best addresses this?

options.text: Keep every tool result forever
options.rationale: Unbounded history worsens context crowding.

options.text: Delegate bounded reviews to isolated subagents and return structured findings
options.rationale: Context isolation preserves main-agent focus while retaining needed evidence.

options.text: Increase randomness
options.rationale: Sampling does not manage context.

options.text: Remove the review criteria
options.rationale: Deleting the goal makes evaluation less reliable.

questions.stem: A sponsor requests a Claude support bot but supplies no volume, latency, data classification, or quality target. What should the developer do before selecting services?

options.text: Choose the largest model immediately
options.rationale: Model selection is premature without functional and infrastructure requirements.

options.text: Extract users, decisions, workload, quality, latency, security, cost, and failure requirements
options.rationale: Implementation choices should follow measurable business and operating constraints.

options.text: Copy an unrelated reference architecture
options.rationale: A reference design cannot replace use-case requirements.

options.text: Promise perfect accuracy
options.rationale: An unsupported guarantee is not a requirement.

questions.stem: A prototype works on a laptop, so the team wants to skip evaluation, deployment review, monitoring, and maintenance ownership. What is missing?

options.text: A standard system life cycle covering validation through operation and change
options.rationale: A production system needs controlled development, release, monitoring, and maintenance.

options.text: A longer product name
options.rationale: Branding does not close lifecycle gaps.

options.text: More prototype-only features
options.rationale: Feature growth increases risk without operational readiness.

options.text: A second laptop
options.rationale: More local hardware is not lifecycle management.

questions.stem: Ten thousand independent documents must be processed overnight at the lowest reasonable API cost. Results are not needed until morning. Which API path fits?

options.text: Synchronous Messages calls from one browser tab
options.rationale: Synchronous calls do not use the cost and scheduling benefits of batch processing.

options.text: Message Batches with stable custom IDs
options.rationale: Batching fits high-volume latency-tolerant work and supports result correlation.

options.text: Streaming every response to a terminal
options.rationale: Streaming improves perceived latency, which this workload does not need.

options.text: One request containing all documents regardless of context limits
options.rationale: Unbounded aggregation can exceed context and makes failures difficult to isolate.

questions.stem: An async TypeScript handler calls a synchronous blocking file parser for every streaming token. What is the likely engineering correction?

options.text: Move blocking work off the event loop and batch it at a defined boundary
options.rationale: Blocking per-token work undermines asynchronous concurrency and streaming responsiveness.

options.text: Increase model temperature
options.rationale: Sampling cannot repair application-level blocking.

options.text: Commit generated secrets to simplify deployment
options.rationale: This introduces a security defect unrelated to concurrency.

options.text: Remove code review
options.rationale: Review helps catch rather than causes the defect.

questions.stem: An API client sends source data inside a user message that also contains untrusted instructions. The system treats both as trusted control text. What design change is strongest?

options.text: Define explicit trusted instruction and untrusted content boundaries, then validate outputs and actions
options.rationale: Clear content boundaries reduce instruction confusion and support enforceable controls.

options.text: Use a more enthusiastic system prompt
options.rationale: Tone does not establish trust boundaries.

options.text: Put every input into one undifferentiated string
options.rationale: This preserves the ambiguity.

options.text: Disable logging only
options.rationale: Logging policy does not separate control from content.

questions.stem: A production app silently moves from one model snapshot to another and quality drops. Which practice best prevents recurrence?

options.text: Pin model and prompt versions, test upgrades against regression evals, and promote intentionally
options.rationale: Versioned configuration makes changes attributable and reversible.

options.text: Always use an unversioned alias without testing
options.rationale: Uncontrolled aliases can introduce behavior changes.

options.text: Store configuration only in one developer's memory
options.rationale: Undocumented state is not reproducible.

options.text: Change model, prompt, and tools together
options.rationale: Bundled changes prevent causal diagnosis.

questions.stem: A repository needs shared build instructions, a security rule only for infrastructure files, and a reusable dependency-audit workflow. Where should these live?

options.text: All in one personal shell alias
options.rationale: Personal aliases are not shared repository configuration.

options.text: CLAUDE.md for shared guidance, path-scoped rules for infrastructure, and a project Skill for the audit
options.rationale: Each Claude Code mechanism matches the intended scope and reuse.

options.text: Only in chat history
options.rationale: Conversation history is not durable team configuration.

options.text: Inside application secrets
options.rationale: Secrets are not an instruction store.

questions.stem: A tool call succeeds, but the final answer omits the tool result. Logs show a valid tool_result was never appended to the next message. Where is the defect?

options.text: The integration loop
options.rationale: The application failed to return tool evidence to the model.

options.text: The model's training data
options.rationale: The missing message is an application trace defect.

options.text: The user's browser theme
options.rationale: Presentation is unrelated to message construction.

options.text: The tool's successful business logic
options.rationale: The tool completed; its result was lost afterward.

questions.stem: Why can two identical Claude requests produce slightly different valid wording?

options.text: LLMs generate token distributions rather than replaying a fixed database row
options.rationale: Probabilistic next-token generation permits variation even with the same prompt.

options.text: The REST protocol randomly edits JSON
options.rationale: REST transport does not rewrite response semantics.

options.text: Context windows guarantee deterministic output
options.rationale: A context window limits available input; it does not guarantee determinism.

options.text: Every response uses a different API schema
options.rationale: Schema stability is separate from generated wording.

questions.stem: A client SDK method returns a promise, but the application reads it as if it were the completed response. What technical concept is missing?

options.text: Asynchronous control flow and awaiting the SDK operation
options.rationale: The wrapped REST call completes asynchronously and must be awaited or handled as a promise.

options.text: Few-shot prompting
options.rationale: Prompt examples do not resolve application control flow.

options.text: Model routing
options.rationale: The call has not been consumed correctly regardless of model.

options.text: Semantic search
options.rationale: Retrieval is unrelated to promise handling.

questions.stem: A low-latency classifier meets its measured target on a smaller model; a complex investigation does not. What routing is defensible?

options.text: Use the smallest model that passes the classifier eval and a more capable model for investigation
options.rationale: Evidence-based routing balances quality, latency, and cost per task.

options.text: Use the largest model for everything without evaluation
options.rationale: This ignores workload-specific tradeoffs.

options.text: Use the smallest model for everything despite failed quality
options.rationale: Cost does not override acceptance criteria.

options.text: Randomly rotate models
options.rationale: Random routing makes performance and cost inconsistent.

questions.stem: Thousands of requests share a long stable policy prefix followed by small user-specific data. Which optimization should be evaluated first?

options.text: Place the stable prefix at the beginning and use prompt caching
options.rationale: A cacheable shared prefix can reduce repeated input cost and latency.

options.text: Repeat the policy after every user sentence
options.rationale: Repetition increases tokens and disrupts a stable prefix.

options.text: Remove token measurement
options.rationale: Without usage data the optimization cannot be validated.

options.text: Increase output limits for all calls
options.rationale: A larger ceiling does not reduce repeated input cost.

questions.stem: A research agent's main context is dominated by raw search pages and no longer follows the task. What is the strongest correction?

options.text: Prune or summarize tool output and isolate bounded searches in subagents
options.rationale: Context engineering retains decision-relevant state while moving bulky exploration out of the main window.

options.text: Add more raw pages indefinitely
options.rationale: More unfiltered context worsens bloat.

options.text: Delete the task criteria
options.rationale: Removing the goal makes drift worse.

options.text: Increase temperature
options.rationale: Sampling does not manage context capacity.

questions.stem: A prompt says 'process this correctly' and the output varies in structure. Which revision is most effective?

options.text: Specify the task, input boundaries, constraints, output contract, and representative examples
options.rationale: Clear instructions and examples reduce ambiguity and make validation possible.

options.text: Repeat correctly in uppercase
options.rationale: Emphasis does not define expected behavior.

options.text: Hide the requested schema
options.rationale: The model needs the output contract.

options.text: Add unrelated background
options.rationale: Irrelevant context dilutes the task.

questions.stem: Claude returns JSON that parses but contains an end date before its start date. What should the application do?

options.text: Accept it because parsing succeeded
options.rationale: Syntax validity does not prove semantic validity.

options.text: Apply schema and semantic validation, then repair or reject with a bounded error path
options.rationale: Defensive output handling checks both structure and business invariants.

options.text: Strip all dates
options.rationale: Removing needed data avoids rather than handles the defect.

options.text: Render the values before validation
options.rationale: Unvalidated output should not enter downstream behavior.

questions.stem: An agent summarizes untrusted web pages and can call an internal delete tool. Which TWO controls address prompt-injection risk?

options.text: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data separated from instructions
options.rationale: Trust separation prevents page text from becoming authoritative control.

options.text: Limit tool authorization and validate sensitive actions outside the model
options.rationale: Least privilege and deterministic checks constrain impact if manipulation occurs.

options.text: Raise temperature
options.rationale: Randomness does not mitigate injection.

options.text: Publish the system prompt
options.rationale: Disclosure does not enforce tool safety.

questions.stem: A public assistant can retrieve records and issue refunds using the same unrestricted credential. What deployment change is strongest?

options.text: Layer input/output controls with separate least-privilege identities and approval for refunds
options.rationale: Defense in depth limits both unsafe content and action authority.

options.text: Add a polite instruction not to misuse tools
options.rationale: Prompt guidance is not an authorization boundary.

options.text: Use one administrator credential everywhere
options.rationale: Broad credentials increase blast radius.

options.text: Remove audit logs
options.rationale: This weakens detection and accountability.

questions.stem: Claude Code must never modify production Terraform during an automated review. Which control provides the required boundary?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that blocks write operations on the protected path
options.rationale: A deterministic hook can deny the action before execution.

options.text: A user message asking Claude to be careful
options.rationale: A prompt cannot guarantee tool enforcement.

options.text: A larger context window
options.rationale: Context capacity does not enforce permissions.

options.text: A higher output token limit
options.rationale: Output length is unrelated to tool safety.

questions.stem: A repository contains a production API key in settings.json so every developer can run the app. What is the correct design?

options.text: Commit the key but obfuscate its name
options.rationale: Renaming does not protect a secret.

options.text: Use an approved secret store, scoped identities, environment injection, rotation, and access monitoring
options.rationale: Secrets should be externalized, least-privileged, and lifecycle managed.

options.text: Share one key in team chat
options.rationale: Shared credentials remove accountability and increase exposure.

options.text: Put the key in CLAUDE.md
options.rationale: Instructions are repository content, not a secret store.

questions.stem: Two tools named lookup and search accept the same string and return different undocumented shapes. Claude frequently chooses incorrectly. What should change first?

options.text: Give each tool a distinct purpose, precise schema, boundaries, examples, and structured errors
options.rationale: Clear interfaces are the primary tool-selection and recovery contract.

options.text: Let Claude call both every time
options.rationale: Duplicate execution adds cost and can create conflicting side effects.

options.text: Remove all descriptions
options.rationale: The model would have less selection evidence.

options.text: Return free-form exceptions only
options.rationale: Unstructured failures weaken recovery.

questions.stem: Several Claude applications need the same independently maintained internal inventory capability. Which implementation best fits?

options.text: Copy REST logic into every application prompt
options.rationale: Prompt copies are not a maintainable integration contract.

options.text: Expose the capability through an MCP server with scoped tools and documented transport
options.rationale: MCP makes reusable capabilities available across compatible clients.

options.text: Paste the inventory into every context
options.rationale: Static copies become stale and waste context.

options.text: Assume built-in tools reach any private API
options.rationale: Built-in tools do not automatically expose arbitrary internal services.

questions.stem: A team wants reusable written deployment guidance that Claude loads when relevant, but it needs no external service call. What mechanism is proportionate?

options.text: A Skill containing the workflow and supporting references
options.rationale: A Skill packages reusable guidance without adding an external tool boundary.

options.text: An MCP server with an empty network service
options.rationale: A server is unnecessary when no external capability is needed.

options.text: A destructive hook
options.rationale: Hooks enforce deterministic events; they are not the primary home for study guidance.

options.text: A custom tool that returns a constant paragraph
options.rationale: A tool adds invocation overhead for static instructions.
